chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who bequeathed more than one-third and freed his slave during his illness, he said: 'If it is more than one-third, it is reduced to one-third, and the manumission is valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bequeathing more than one-third of an estate in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the independent validity of manumission (itq) even when the bequest portion is reduced to the statutory one-third limit, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the concurrence of will and emancipation. It reflects the principle that the slave's freedom is not contingent upon the full execution of the bequest, ensuring the slave's status is secured despite the reduction in estate distribution. This ruling underscores the balance between the rights of heirs and the merit of freeing a slave in the final illness (marad al-maut).
